text:
Maya: Quick sync — proposing a lightweight graceful-degradation pattern for edge ownership and tenant locality. Goal: keep preferred-region affinity but allow controlled, auditable fallbacks for reads when latency or capacity breaches SLOs.

Sanjay: +1. Do we have an explicit opt-in per-tenant for fallback? must avoid accidental residency violations.

Maya: Yes — tenants declare a residency profile: STRICT, PREFERRED, FLEX. Only PREFERRED/FLEX allow cross-region read fallbacks; STRICT stays pinned and will surface errors.

Omar: How do you envision ownership transfer? short lease or heartbeat? we should avoid split-brain on active/active writes.

Maya: Lease with tombstone+grace window. ownership lease is soft: holders renew every 15s, TTL 30s. On conflict, prefer region with lower write age + canary check. Writes always require a local write lease; cross-region writes are disallowed unless tenant is FLEX.

Liz: Important: audit trail and consent. Need metadata on the request showing fallback reason + origin region for compliance. Also provide an opt-out toggle in the console.

Talia: KV cache implications: if fallback serves reads from cached KV, we must invalidate on write or scope cache by residency tag. Can't leak data between residency groups.

Omar: Agreed. Cache keys need residency namespace, e.g. `tenant:<id>:residency:<region>:kv`. Also keep a `last-write-region` header on responses.

Maya: Prototype config (for discussion):
```yaml
residency_policy:
  preferred: eu-west-1
  fallbacks:
    - eu-central-1  # read-only fallback
    - us-west-2     # metadata / degraded probes only
  mode: PREFERRED
  lease_ttl: 30s
  grace_window: 90s
```

Sanjay: For failover exercises, can we simulate fallback without enabling it? a dry-run flag would be helpful (`dry_run=true` logs decisions but doesn't route).

Maya: Yes — add `dry_run` on the tenant policy and to the routing layer. We'll log intended fallback decisions to the audit stream.

infra-bot: New runbook created: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/edge-degrade-v1 (auto-generated from draft).

Liz: One more: telemetry. We need token-level metrics: fallback_count, avg_fallback_latency, compliance_violations. Tie alerts to `fallback_count > threshold`.

Omar: Implementation notes: router should be policy-first, then capacity-aware. Policy = residency constraints, then capacity/cost opt. If capacity fails and tenant is PREFERRED, attempt fallbacks in order with `read-only` flag.

Talia: For KV sync: if fallback region serves read-only, we should allow async replication for eventual locality catch-up, but writes remain canonical in owner region until explicit handoff.

Maya: Action items: 1) I'll draft RFC with lease state machine + API for `residency_profile` (due EOD Fri). 2) @Sanjay to add dry-run wiring in the simulator. 3) @Omar/Talia to sketch cache namespace + replication constraints. 4) @Liz to enumerate compliance metadata fields.

Sanjay: Ack. I'll add a small harness to flip `dry_run` per-tenant so QA can run failover scenarios.

Omar: I'll prototype lease conflict resolution (prefer oldest write age, fall back to canary when ambiguous).

Liz: I'll draft the compliance checklist items and console UI wording.

Maya: Thanks — ping me if anything blocks. Plan to merge RFC into `multi-region-refactors` branch after reviews. :white_check_mark:
